description: Conformance corpus for isolation between mods sharing one runtime. Mod `a` is loaded and registers handlers at load time; mod `b` is loaded next with a case's `tamper` as its entry source; then mod `a`'s `setup` export registers a second set of handlers. Whatever `b` attempted, every step in `steps` must still hold: `a`'s handlers all run with their own results, its exports resolve to its own functions, host bindings it calls answer as the host wrote them, its console output reaches the host, and nothing `b` did let it read `a`'s functions or the runtime's internals.
notes: Per case: create a runtime from `host` granting no capabilities, with the host functions `log(x)` returning "log:" + x and `ns.get(x)` returning "get:" + x, and a console handler that records every call. Load `a.manifest` with `a.source` as its entry script. Run `internals` as host code; its value must equal `[]`, since no runtime leaves a global whose name starts with `__xript` where a script can see it. Then load `b` (manifest `b`, entry source the case's `tamper`). Loading `b` may fail: a tamper that throws at declaration is still a tamper, and the runner ignores the failure. Then invoke `a`'s `setup` export through the owned-export entry point, clear the recorded console calls, and run `steps` in order.

Step kinds. `{ fire, phase?, data, expected }`: the host fires hook `fire` (at `phase` when present) with `data` as the one payload value; the results equal `expected`. `{ fragment, lifecycle, ops }`: the host fires the fragment hook and receives `ops` operations. `{ invoke, mod, expected }`: the host invokes export `invoke` of mod `mod`; the result equals `expected`. `{ invoke, mod, logs }`: as before, and afterwards the console calls recorded since the last clear are exactly `logs`, each a single string argument (a JavaScript runtime's handler) or that string as the message (a runtime whose handler receives text). `{ emit, payload, expected }`: the host emits event `emit` with the one payload value; the handler results equal `expected`. `{ execute, expected }`: host code whose value equals `expected`.

`steps` is shared by every case. The last step reads `globalThis.stolen`, which several tampers set to whatever they managed to read. `b` registers no handler of its own in any case, so every result list holds only `a`'s.
Each tamper wraps its attempts in `try`, so a refused attempt does not stop the next one, except where the attempt is the declaration itself.

A runtime defends against a monkeypatched built-in by capturing the built-ins its own sandbox-side code calls when it installs that code, before any script runs, and never looking one up again. It defends against a rewritten global by keeping its internals in closures rather than on `globalThis`, and by installing the bindings, `hooks`, `events`, `xript`, and `console` globals as non-writable, non-configurable properties of frozen objects.

setup.description: Registers a second set of handlers.

debugCase.name: replace a debug probe
debugCase.description: A runtime whose debugger instruments host code installs probe globals the instrumented code calls by name, so while a debug session is attached they are the one exception to `internals`. Run this case like any other but with a debug session attached and without the `internals` check: record `probes` as host code after loading `a`, load `b` with `tamper`, run `setup` and `steps`, then `probes` must evaluate to the same list and `locked` to `[]`. A runtime whose debugger installs no globals sees an empty list and passes. A runtime that can debug only in one of its modes runs this case in that mode.
debugCase.probes: (function () { var names = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(globalThis); var found = []; for (var i = 0; i < names.length; i++) { if (names[i].slice(0, 7) === '__xript') found.push(names[i]); } return found.sort(); })()
debugCase.locked: (function () { var names = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(globalThis); var open = []; for (var i = 0; i < names.length; i++) { if (names[i].slice(0, 7) !== '__xript') continue; var d = Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(globalThis, names[i]); if (d.configurable || d.writable === true || d.set) open.push(names[i]); } return open; })()

internals: (function () { var names = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(globalThis); var found = []; for (var i = 0; i < names.length; i++) { if (names[i].slice(0, 7) === '__xript') found.push(names[i]); } return found; })()

cases.name: assign over a top-level binding
cases.tamper:
try { log = function () { return 'evil'; }; } catch (e) {}
try { globalThis.log = function () { return 'evil'; }; } catch (e) {}

cases.name: delete a top-level binding
cases.tamper:
try { delete globalThis.log; } catch (e) {}
try { delete globalThis.ns; } catch (e) {}

cases.name: redefine a top-level binding
cases.tamper: try { Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'log', { value: function () { return 'evil'; }, writable: true, configurable: true }); } catch (e) {}

cases.name: declare a global function over a binding
cases.tamper: function log() { return 'evil'; }

cases.name: declare a global variable over a binding
cases.tamper: var log = function () { return 'evil'; };

cases.name: replace a namespace
cases.tamper:
try { globalThis.ns = { get: function () { return 'evil'; } }; } catch (e) {}
try { Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'ns', { value: { get: function () { return 'evil'; } } }); } catch (e) {}

cases.name: rewrite a namespace member
cases.tamper:
try { ns.get = function () { return 'evil'; }; } catch (e) {}
try { Object.defineProperty(ns, 'get', { value: function () { return 'evil'; } }); } catch (e) {}

cases.name: replace the hooks object
cases.tamper:
try { globalThis.hooks = { tick: function () {}, save: { pre: function () {} }, fragment: { update: function () {} } }; } catch (e) {}
try { Object.defineProperty(globalThis, 'hooks', { value: { tick: function () {}, save: { pre: function () {} }, fragment: { update: function () {} } } }); } catch (e) {}

replace the xript namespace
replace the events object
cases.tamper:
try { events.on = function () {}; } catch (e) {}
try { globalThis.events = { on: function () {}, emit: function () {}, subscribe: function () {} }; } catch (e) {}

cases.name: replace the console
cases.tamper:
try { console.log = function () {}; } catch (e) {}
try { globalThis.console = { log: function () {}, info: function () {} }; } catch (e) {}

cases.name: read the runtime's internals
cases.tamper: var names = Object.getOwnPropertyNames(globalThis); var found = []; for (var i = 0; i < names.length; i++) { if (names[i].slice(0, 7) === '__xript') found.push(names[i]); } if (found.length > 0) globalThis.stolen = found;

replace every internal helper
forge the export owner

cases.tamper: try { Array.prototype.push = function () { globalThis.stolen = arguments[0]; return 0; }; } catch (e) {}
